task: Close checker-authority gaps for record == and Char/String equality so every checker-accepted program runs or is rejected before execution
observation: The checker's equality case only rejected enum and mismatched Range operands, so 'Point == Point', '1 == "a"', and even juxtaposed operands such as 'x = foo bar' or 'x = if c: 1 else: 2' passed moss check and then failed in rustc and Fast Debug. The failure surfaced as a generated-Rust E0369/E0308 or an interpreter 'unsupported expression', far from the Moss line that caused it.
impact: An agent trusting moss check --json would have been told an invalid program was valid; diagnosis required reading generated Rust, which the workflow tells agents not to do. New diagnostics RECORD_EQUALITY_UNSUPPORTED, TYPE_MISMATCH, and INVALID_EXPRESSION now report the Moss line before any engine runs.
evidence: ./moss check <program with a == b on a record> --json (ok:true before the fix)

resolution.summary: Checker rules added with three-engine and diagnostic regressions; a repo-wide moss check diff over 1831 .moss files against the starting compiler showed only intended Char/String migrations.

task: Write Char(Int) boundary tests for the final Char/String contract
observation: Expected Char(128512).to_string().length() to type as Int. The checker reported 'invalid builtin operation char.length' because parse_simple_call accepted 'Char(65).to_string()' as a call of Char whose single argument was the text '65).to_string('. Binding the to_string() result to a local first did not help, since that local was also typed Char.
impact: A natural chained expression on a constructor result was rejected with a misleading type; the same helper is used for every builtin-call typing decision, so other callee(...).method() chains were exposed to the same misparse.
evidence: echo Char(65).to_string().length()  # TYPE_MISMATCH before the fix

resolution.summary: parse_simple_call now requires the callee's opening parenthesis to close at the final ')'; the repo-wide check diff was unchanged.
